title: A network of rings reads its genus: two rings of cuts per handle keep one piece
subject: Networks of rings joined by shared contacts, read with the canonical knot test on their space-time law
conclusion: In any network of rule-60 rings, the pieces read from which uncut contacts need which rings after a cut are exactly the components of the ring graph without the cut contacts. So a family of rings of cuts keeps the network in one piece exactly when it is independent in the surface's homology mod 2, which allows at most two per handle, as on the torus and on a persistent genus-2 network of 16 rings.
